findings.title: Approved live builds fail the fixture-only browser gate
findings.why_it_matters: A merchant's valid approved public build cannot pass hosted full validation when its catalog or origin differs from the committed fallback fixture. The new public input survives production-builds/static-output, but the following browser gate reuses that output with the unchanged suite that requires Atlas Carry-on, Fixture variants, Select variant, and shop.example.invalid URLs. A browser gate selected from the same immutable public input would validate the actual frozen content without replacing it with a fixture build.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a public-build browser configuration/suite that derives product routes, names and canonical origin from the retained approved input, and select it for publication validation while reusing the exact generated output. Preserve the public input/theme selector for that gate; keep the existing fixture-specific fallback tests on their own fixture build, rather than rebuilding the delivery artifact to satisfy them. Verify this with an approved input whose product slug and site.origin differ from the committed fixture.

findings.title: Public staging proof selects fallback and private-journey tests
findings.why_it_matters: Even after validation is repaired, a correctly deployed public Fashion Store cannot pass the selected hosted purchase proof. The root suite's mandatory purchase project clicks the fallback Add to bag button and expects automatic navigation to /cart, while the public live page uses Add to cart and keeps the customer on the product page. Its Fashion purchase project is a private-preview journey that skips without FASHION_U12_PHASE, and the remaining root operations tests require fixture variables that this job never supplies; the delivery runner therefore restores the old version instead of recording activation.
findings.suggested_fix: Select a hosted public-live purchase proof for this job, binding it to the retained Catalog/Snapshot and using the Fashion Store's actual option selection, Add to cart action and cart navigation. Supply/prepare only the staging Commerce data and required operational fixture variables that the selected tests need, under the existing REL staging authority. Do not use the private-preview FASHION_U12 grant flow or the fallback-specific purchase project as proof of public publication; add a workflow integration check covering the selected configuration and its required environment.

findings.title: Every publication fails the rehearsal-only latency authority check
findings.why_it_matters: Any publication that reaches the latency command is rejected before a latency request is made. That tool requires the protected CI-GH rollback-rehearsal authority, including CI_GH_STAGING_REHEARSAL=true, CI_GH_PRODUCTION_PROMOTION=false and the validated SHA; the new publication job supplies none of these, and publication preflight explicitly forbids a rollback rehearsal. This rolls back a successful staging publication and blocks every production publication's staging proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide a dedicated formal-publication entry point for the shared latency probe, with authority checks for the protected deploy workflow, exact validated SHA, staging activation target, publication identity and same run. Invoke that entry point from publication-staging while leaving the existing CI-GH rehearsal-only entry point and its guards intact; do not fabricate rehearsal flags to bypass its intentionally different authority. Add a non-network authority test using the actual publication job environment.

findings.title: Pre-delivery job failure permanently strands the pending publication
findings.why_it_matters: An ordinary job failure before delivery, such as a staging browser installation failure or a production backup rejection, leaves the request marked building although no storefront mutation occurred. The workflow's finalizer excludes staging-source publication-staging failures and any publication-production failure, while the runner's recovery catch begins only after baseline loading/rechecking. Admin consequently keeps showing publishing and refuses another request because the environment's unique pending row never becomes failed; cases before capture also lack the baseline required by the documented recovery command.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the capture/deliver steps explicit IDs and finalize unsuccessful publication jobs that never entered a mutation-capable delivery step, using the same-run failed callback and the producer's existing current-storefront verification. Cover publication-staging for staging-source requests and publication-production pre-delivery failures; keep post-mutation/unknown outcomes on the existing retained-baseline unresolved recovery path. Add workflow/state integration scenarios for browser-install failure, backup rejection and baseline-capture failure, verifying that a safely failed request permits a new attempt and an unverifiable storefront remains unresolved.
